title: Pasqal Transitions €50 Million Q-PLANET Pilot Line into Execution Phase for European Neutral-Atom Chips - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Neutral-atom quantum hardware provider Pasqal (NASDAQ: PSQL) has announced the transition of the Q-PLANET (Quantum Pilot Line for production of Advanced chips for Neutral atom European Technologies) initiative into its operational execution phase. Three months following its kick-off meeting in Brussels, Pasqal is leading a 28-partner consortium spanning 11 European countries to construct a domestic semiconductor and photonic supply chain for neutral-atom quantum computing, sensing, and communications.

Co-funded with €50 million (~$57.2 million USD) over three years by the European Union’s Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU) alongside national and regional agencies (including France 2030, ERDF, Business Finland, FFG, and the Ministry of Science, Research and Arts Baden-Württemberg), Q-PLANET targets the industrialization of chip-scale components. Technical deliverables focus on developing integrated laser sources across four critical optical wavelengths (461 nm, 698 nm, 795 nm, and 1013 nm), atom chips for quantum processors and sensors, microfabricated vapor cells for atomic clocks, and standardized Process Design Kits (PDKs) and Assembly Design Kits (ADKs) for commercial semiconductor foundries.

Pasqal serves as both lead project coordinator and end-user validator for microfabricated vapor cells and laser sources integrated across its neutral-atom quantum processing units (QPUs). The initiative establishes standardized manufacturing processes to accelerate industrialization, supporting upcoming European quantum infrastructure deployments across HPC supercomputing centers (TGCC, Forschungszentrum Jülich, CINECA) and commercial sectors including drug discovery and advanced materials science.
